chat.content: Sunlight is scattered by gas molecules in the atmosphere, and shorter wavelengths scatter far more strongly than longer ones (Rayleigh scattering, ∝ 1/λ⁴). Blue light scatters roughly five times more than red, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet, so the diffuse light reaching us from every direction in the sky appears blue.
